newsitem.title: USA: Steel Dynamics revises credit pact, sees Q3 charge.
newsitem.headline: Steel Dynamics revises credit pact, sees Q3 charge.

text.p: Steel Dynamics Inc said Thursday it revised a 1994 credit agreement and will take a charge against earnings of about $10.7 million after taxes to cover a write-off of unamortized financing costs associated with the original 1994 agreement.
This charge will be reflected as an extraordinary item in the third quarter 1997 results, the company said in a news release.
The revision increases the facility to $450 million from $345 million, extends its final maturity through the second quarter of 2004, and reduces the company's interest costs.
Steel Dynamics said the additional funds will allow the company to pursue growth opportunities and provides needed flexibility.
Steel Dynamics provides flat-rolled steel products, including light gauge micro-alloyed and high strength steels for the automotive market.

The agreement includes a group of 12 banks with Mellon Bank as the agent, Kreditanstalt fur Wiederaufbau and Comerica Bank as senior co-agents, and Banque Nationale de Paris, The Industrial Bank of Japan and NBD Bank as co-agents for this agreement.
